narr: Abundant moisture (PWATs 1.7-2.0) and instability (MUCAPE 2,000 J/kg) provided a favorable environment for strong to severe thunderstorms across south-central Arizona on the 14th. Daytime heating aided in thunderstorm development across the high terrain north of Phoenix before sending outflows traveling toward the south into the lower elevations. New thunderstorm development occurred along these outflows into the Valley where they produced damaging winds, dense blowing dust, and isolated flash flooding. Additional thunderstorm development occurred across southwest Arizona where better moisture allowed thunderstorms to be efficient rainfall producers, leading to multiple reports of flash flooding. No injuries were reported from this event.
ev: ADOT reported that SR 95 was closed due to flooding near milepost 80. There were also reports of a couple of cars that attempted to cross the flooded road but were not able to make it across and had to be pulled out. No injuries were reported.
ADOT reported that SR 238 was closed due to flooding. No damage or injuries were reported.
Images showed parts of Alamo Road washed out due to high flow over low water crossings. Timing and exact location estimated from radar. No injuries were reported.

A video showed a flood wave traveling down Pinal Creek in Six Shooter Canyon before overtopping a bridge along Six Shooter Canyon Road. Flood waters could be seen traveling down the road making the road impassable. No damage or injuries were reported.
Washes were reported to be running across SR 72 and McVay Road, causing impacts to the roadways. No damage or injuries were reported.
Multiple instances of flooding were reported along SR 95 south of Quartzsite, impacting travel on the roadway. No injuries were reported.
SR 95 north of Quartzsite was closed due to flooding. No damage or injuries were reported.

The FCDMC streamflow gage along 4th of July Wash exceeded alarm stage, impacting a downstream low water crossing along Agua Caliente Road. The gage peaked at a depth of 0.74 feet. No damage or injuries were reported.
